method.title: How the calculator estimates materials
method.intro: The estimate uses common Indian civil-engineering thumb rules for a residential RCC-frame house, applied to your built-up area and number of floors. Footings are added per column, with one column roughly every 12 ft in each direction.
rules: Cement: 0.45 bags (50 kg) per sq ft of built-up area per floor (thumb rule 0.40–0.45), plus 4 bags per column footing.
Steel (sariya): 3.3 kg per sq ft (thumb rule 3.0–3.5 kg), plus 50 kg per column footing.
Sand (balu): 1.1 cft per sq ft (thumb rule 1.0–1.2 cft), plus about 7.5 cft per footing.
Gitti (aggregate): 1.6 cft per sq ft (thumb rule 1.5–1.7 cft), plus about 14.5 cft per footing.
Bricks: about 7.5 bricks per sq ft of built-up area.
method.example: About 450 bags of cement, 3,300 kg of steel, 1,100 cft of sand, 1,600 cft of gitti and 7,500 bricks, before footings. A civil engineer should confirm final quantities for your design.
